skills.trigger: When evaluating serial chest radiographs in a patient with known fibrocystic lung disease (e.g., sarcoidosis, TB) to identify interval changes suggestive of superimposed pathology.
steps: Compare the baseline and follow-up images side-by-side, focusing specifically on areas of pre-existing upper lobe fibrosis or cavitation.
Identify any new or increasing opacity that is pleural-based or located within a pre-existing cavity, distinguishing it from stable fibrotic scarring by its increased density or mass-like appearance.

Correlate the finding of a new dense opacity within a cystic space with the clinical context to suggest mycetoma (fungus ball) formation, rather than assuming it represents progression of fibrosis alone.
